:::{#thm-affine-map-unique}
#### An affine map determines its matrix and offset

If an [affine map](#def-affine-map) $f$ satisfies
$f(\vx) = \matr{A}\vx + \vec{b}$ and $f(\vx) = \matr{A}'\vx + \vec{b}'$
[for all](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-universal-quantifier) $\vx \in \reals^p$,
then the two [formulas](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/expressions-algorithms.html#def-closed-form-expression) have the same [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) and the same [offset](#def-affine-offset):

$$
\matr{A}' = \matr{A}
\quad \text{and} \quad
\vec{b}' = \vec{b}.
$$ {#eq-affine-map-unique}

:::

::: proof

By @thm-affine-map-zero, applied to each formula,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\vec{b} &= f(\vzero) \\
&= \vec{b}'.
\end{aligned}
$$

Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{A}\vx &= f(\vx) - \vec{b} \\
&= \matr{A}'\vx
\end{aligned}
$$

for all $\vx$,
so $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{A}'$ are both matrices (@def-matrix-of-linear-map) of the linear map
$\vx \mapsto f(\vx) - \vec{b}$ (linear by @thm-matrix-map-linear),
and the uniqueness in @thm-linear-map-matrix gives $\matr{A}' = \matr{A}$.

:::
